correctness.rationale: For odd n>=3, the homomorphism equation after subtracting f(0) gives h(-x)=-h(x), h(2y)=2h(y), and h(2y+x)=h(2y)+h(x). Surjectivity of doubling gives additivity and hence the affine normal form. Direct composition gives determinant adjacency in (a-1,b) coordinates. At n=p^e a unit coordinate lets one solve the single determinant equation uniquely along the primitive line, which is a complete closed neighborhood. For e=1 remove all nonzero points and then the singleton; at e>=2 the remaining points px are partitioned into fibers labelled by x mod p^{e-2}. These labels are well defined, each fiber is a p^2-clique, and two different fibers have uniform complete or empty adjacency by cancellation of p^2 in the determinant congruence. Lifting a base perfect-elimination order one fiber at a time gives a perfect-elimination order because every later neighbor lies in the same fiber or in a later neighboring fiber, and the latter labels form a clique. This includes e=2 via the one-vertex modulus-one base. The same argument bounds the largest core clique by p^2 times the base clique number; a primitive line attains p^e and reverse greedy coloring is optimal in each induced graph. For other odd moduli coprime nontrivial factors give orthogonal idempotents: the four listed vertices have zero determinants exactly on the four cycle edges, since the diagonal pairs have determinants equal to the nonzero idempotents. Replayed python3 /workspace/repairs/4/verify.py and observed VERIFY_OK affine=3,5 orders=3,5,9,25,27 cycles=15,21,45. These checks are finite: exhaustive endomorphisms at 3 and 5, all-pair affine commutation and later-neighbor clique tests at the five prime powers, and four-cycle tests on the listed composite moduli. The provided frozen verifier was inspected but not executed. The repaired proof makes no assertion at even moduli or about the chromatic number at mixed-prime moduli.

exact_database_or_table.reasoning: With C_e the originally claimed determinant polynomial, the triangular polynomial equals C_e((1+z)^{p^e}-1). Undoing the substitution gives S_e(1+z)^{p^e}-(S_e-1)(1+z)^{p^{e-1}}. This satisfies the frozen recurrence: the primitive contribution adds p^{e-1}(p+1)=S_e-S_{e-2} to the leading coefficient and subtracts it from the other coefficient; the e=2 core term uses the one-vertex base. Thus the all-size table/formula is exactly covered. Clique counts or tuple counts alone do not include an elimination order or induced-cycle classification; the retained boundary is a different invariant.

value.rationale: The repaired theorem classifies a natural commuting graph at every odd modulus and gives a usable constructive elimination and coloring procedure on the positive side. It distinguishes complete neighborhoods at primitive vertices from the recursively structured nonprimitive remainder; on the negative side it gives an explicit minimal-length forbidden induced cycle. This is structural information absent from the exact clique census alone.
